crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers the use of overhead images to measure physical activity that shows up in economic or environmental indicators.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data covers aggregated and anonymized records of consumer purchases made with credit and debit cards, including point of sale, online, and mobile payments.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data covers the digital exhaust of physical movement: vessel positions from AIS, port call records, container and bulk cargo manifests where available, terminal gate and crane activity, truck and rail telematics, and fixed or mobile IoT sensors on assets and in facilities.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone or tablet has been, inferred from GPS, Wi-Fi, cell tower and beacon signals.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services for use as alternative data.

sections.body: Alternative data in AI economics means using non-traditional digital traces to measure economic activity, consumer behavior, supply chains, and environmental conditions. Satellite imagery lets models estimate things like parking lot occupancy, crop health, construction progress, and emissions without waiting for official reports. Card transaction data gives a near real time view of spending by category, merchant, and region, though it is a sample and not a census. Sensor and shipping data track goods moving through ports, trucks, rails, and warehouses, and they can reveal bottlenecks before statistics agencies publish. Mobile location data shows foot traffic to stores, offices, and events, and web data collection gathers prices, job postings, reviews, and other public signals. In practice, AI is used to clean, align, and combine these messy streams, then to forecast or nowcast economic indicators.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is mature in some narrow tasks, such as extracting vehicle counts from satellite images or classifying merchant categories from card records. It is not solved as a general measurement problem, because each source has coverage gaps, sampling bias, and changing collection methods. Satellite imagery struggles with clouds, resolution limits, and the cost of labeling, while card data may miss cash purchases and underrepresent certain groups. Location data depends on app permissions and privacy rules, and web collection must handle blocking, layout changes, and duplicate listings. Shipping and sensor data can be precise for tracked assets but incomplete for informal or small scale trade. The honest limit is that alternative data often produces useful signals, not definitive totals, and validation against official statistics remains necessary.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section follow the main data families, and for readers connecting these sources to public markets, the site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices. Satellite Imagery covers overhead observation and the computer vision methods used to turn pixels into economic indicators. Card Transaction Data deals with spending records, panel construction, and the gap between a sample and total consumer activity. Sensor and Shipping Data looks at physical movement through ports, logistics networks, and industrial equipment. Mobile Location Data examines foot traffic, mobility patterns, and the privacy questions that shape what can be collected and used. Web Data Collection covers scraping, APIs, and the extraction of prices, listings, and text from public pages, and together these pages show how AI turns scattered digital exhaust into economic evidence, and where that evidence remains partial.
